items.readable_text:
Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/1265bc68fc54501abac991d267434ac6]

Content:
The polar curve shown above is defined as
[MATH: r(\theta) = 4 - 3\cos \theta, \qquad 0\leq \theta < 2\pi.]

Content:
We have [MATH: \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}] at the point [MATH: P.] The tangent to the curve at [MATH: P] is shown in the diagram.

Content:
To find the equation of the tangent line to the curve at [MATH: P,] we follow four steps.

Content:
Step 1: Calculate the derivative [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}.]

Content:
Using techniques that we've previously discussed, we can show that

Content:
[MATH: y^{′}(θ) = 4\cos θ − 3\cos 2θ, x^{′}(θ) = 3\sin 2θ − 4\sin θ.]

Content:
Therefore, we can find [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: (dy)/(dx)|= (y^{′}(θ))/(x^{′}(θ)); = (4\cos θ − 3\cos 2θ)/(3\sin 2θ − 4\sin θ)]

Content:
Step 2: Find the slope of the tangent at [MATH: P.]

Content:
The slope of the tangent line is

Content:
[MATH: m|= (dy)/(dx)|_{θ = π/2}; = (4\cos ((π)/(2)) − 3\cos (2 ⋅ (π)/(2)))/(3\sin (2 ⋅ (π)/(2)) − 4\sin ((π)/(2))); = (4\cos ((π)/(2)) − 3\cos (π))/(3\sin (π) − 4\sin ((π)/(2))); = (0 + 3)/(0 − 4); = − (3)/(4).]

Content:
Step 3: Find the Cartesian coordinates of [MATH: P.]

Content:
We compute the [MATH: xy]-coordinates of [MATH: P] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: x_{1}|= r\cos θ; = (4 − 3\cos θ)\cos θ; = (4 − 3\cos ((π)/(2)))\cos ((π)/(2)); = 0; y_{1}|= r\sin θ; = (4 − 3\cos θ)\sin θ; = (4 − 3\cos ((π)/(2)))\sin ((π)/(2)); = 4]

Content:
Therefore, the coordinates of [MATH: P] are [MATH: \left( 0, 4 \right).]

Content:
Step 4: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the tangent.

Content:
We find the equation of the tangent as follows:

Content:
[MATH: y − y_{1}|= m(x − x_{1}); y − 4|= − (3)/(4) ⋅ (x − 0); y|= − (3)/(4)x + 4]

Find the equation of the tangent line to the polar curve [MATH: r = 1+2\cos\theta] at [MATH: \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2},] given that

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x} = -\dfrac{\cos\theta + 2\cos(2\theta)}{\sin\theta + 2\sin(2\theta)}.]
sections.readable_text:
Find the equation of the tangent line to the polar curve [MATH: r = 1+2\cos\theta] at [MATH: \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2},] given that

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x} = -\dfrac{\cos\theta + 2\cos(2\theta)}{\sin\theta + 2\sin(2\theta)}.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To find the equation of the tangent line to a polar curve at a point [MATH: P,] we follow four steps:

Step 1: Calculate the derivative [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}.]

In this case, we're given that

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x} = -\dfrac{\cos\theta + 2\cos(2\theta)}{\sin\theta + 2\sin(2\theta)}.]

Step 2: Find the slope of the tangent at [MATH: P.]

The slope of the tangent line is

[MATH: m|= (dy)/(dx)|_{θ = π/2}; = − (\cos ((π)/(2)) + 2\cos (π))/(\sin ((π)/(2)) + 2\sin (π)); = − (0 + 2(− 1))/(1 + 2(0)); = 2.]

Step 3: Find the Cartesian coordinates of [MATH: P.]

We compute the [MATH: xy]-coordinates of [MATH: P] as follows:

[MATH: x_{1}|= r\cos θ; = (1 + 2\cos θ)\cos θ; = (1 + 2\cos ((π)/(2)))\cos ((π)/(2)); = (1 + 2 ⋅ 0) ⋅ 0; = 0; y_{1}|= r\sin θ; = (1 + 2\cos θ)\sin θ; = (1 + 2\cos ((π)/(2)))\sin ((π)/(2)); = (1 + 2 ⋅ 0) ⋅ 1; = 1 ⋅ 1; = 1]

Therefore, the coordinates of [MATH: P] are [MATH: (0,1).]

Step 4: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the tangent.

We find the equation of the tangent as follows:

[MATH: y − y_{1}|= m(x − x_{1}); y − 1|= 2(x − 0); y|= 2x + 1]

sections.normalized_html: Find the equation of the normal line to the polar curve [MATH: r = 1 - 2\cos\theta] at [MATH: \theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{2},] given that [MATH: y'(\theta) = \cos\theta-2\cos(2\theta) , \qquad x'(\theta) = 2\sin(2\theta) - \sin\theta.]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/cedada86002832a7b352cc49dec2ab3b]

Find the equation of the normal line to the polar curve [MATH: r = 1 - 2\cos\theta] at [MATH: \theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{2},] given that
[MATH: y'(\theta) = \cos\theta-2\cos(2\theta) , \qquad
x'(\theta) = 2\sin(2\theta) - \sin\theta.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To find the equation of the normal line to a polar curve at a point [MATH: P,] we follow four steps:

Step 1: Calculate the derivative [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}.]

In this case, we're given that

[MATH: y'(\theta) = \cos\theta-2\cos(2\theta) , \qquad x'(\theta) = 2\sin(2\theta) - \sin\theta.]

Therefore,

[MATH: (dy)/(dx)|= (y^{′}(θ))/(x^{′}(θ)); = (\cos θ − 2\cos (2θ))/(2\sin (2θ) − \sin θ)]

Step 2: Find the slope of the tangent at [MATH: P.]

The slope of the tangent line is

[MATH: m|= (dy)/(dx)|_{θ = 3π/2}; = ((\cos ((3π)/(2)) − 2\cos (2 ⋅ (3π)/(2))))/((2\sin (2 ⋅ (3π)/(2)) − \sin ((3π)/(2)))); = ((\cos ((3π)/(2)) − 2\cos (3π)))/((2\sin (3π) − \sin ((3π)/(2)))); = (0 − 2(− 1))/(0 − (− 1)); = (0 + 2)/(0 + 1); = 2.]

Step 3: Find the Cartesian coordinates of [MATH: P.]

We compute the [MATH: xy]-coordinates of [MATH: P] as follows:

[MATH: x_{1}|= r\cos θ; = (1 − 2\cos θ)\cos θ; = (1 − 2\cos ((3π)/(2)))\cos ((3π)/(2)); = (1 − 2 ⋅ 0) ⋅ 0; = 0; y_{1}|= r\sin θ; = (1 − 2\cos θ)\sin θ; = (1 − 2\cos ((3π)/(2)))\sin ((3π)/(2)); = (1 − 2 ⋅ 0) ⋅ (− 1); = 1 ⋅ (− 1); = − 1]

Therefore, the coordinates of [MATH: P] are [MATH: \left( 0, -1 \right).]

Step 4: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the normal.

We find the equation of the normal as follows:

[MATH: y − y_{1}|= − (1)/(m)(x − x_{1}); y − (− 1)|= − (1)/(2) ⋅ (x − 0); y + 1|= − (1)/(2)x; y|= − (1)/(2)x − 1]

To find the equation of the tangent line to a polar curve at a point [MATH: P,] we follow four steps:

Step 1: Calculate the derivative [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}.]

In this case, we're given that

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x} = -\dfrac{\cos\theta + 2\cos(2\theta)}{\sin\theta + 2\sin(2\theta)}.]

Step 2: Find the slope of the tangent at [MATH: P.]

[MATH: m|= (dy)/(dx)|_{θ = π/2}; = − (\cos ((π)/(2)) + 2\cos (π))/(\sin ((π)/(2)) + 2\sin (π)); = − (0 + 2(− 1))/(1 + 2(0)); = 2.]

[MATH: x_{1}|= r\cos θ; = (1 + 2\cos θ)\cos θ; = (1 + 2\cos ((π)/(2)))\cos ((π)/(2)); = (1 + 2 ⋅ 0) ⋅ 0; = 0; y_{1}|= r\sin θ; = (1 + 2\cos θ)\sin θ; = (1 + 2\cos ((π)/(2)))\sin ((π)/(2)); = (1 + 2 ⋅ 0) ⋅ 1; = 1 ⋅ 1; = 1]
